correctness.rationale: All pure states of an ensemble of the rank-two density lie in its GHZ/W range. The HJW co-isometry has weights p_j=lambda|v_1j|²+(1-lambda)|v_2j|² and r_j=|v_1j|²/p_j with sum p_jr_j=1. The given pure objective is g(r)=(5lambda²r²-4lambda r+8)/9 with g''=10lambda²/9>0; strict Jensen equality forces all r_j=1, then |v_1j|²=|v_2j|²=p_j. Orthogonal co-isometry rows are precisely the phase zero-barycenter condition. Conversely it yields a valid row isometry and equality. Minimum rank-two ensemble size >=2, and a two-vector zero barycenter forces 1/2 weights and antipodal phases. Direct independent complex-amplitude density-matrix calculations evaluated 4det rho_A at six lambda values and four phases each; phase-independence and polynomial matched. The strict Jensen argument proves all lambda, not finite samples.
residual_risks: Depends on exact concurrence-fill pure-state formula and rank-two HJW parametrization for canonical orthogonal GHZ/W pair; these were checked algebraically but main source primary PDF remained unavailable.
The parameter endpoints lambda=0,1 are excluded because rho becomes pure.

final_claim: For 0<lambda<1 in the canonical GHZ/W rank-two mixture, every finite concurrence-fill-convex-roof optimal decomposition comprises states sqrt(lambda)GHZ+e^{i theta_j}sqrt(1-lambda)W with positive probabilities summing one and sum p_j e^{i theta_j}=0. Minimum support is two with equal weights and opposite phases, and the roof value remains (5lambda²-4lambda+8)/9.
limitations: Canonical orthonormal GHZ/W mixture with 0<lambda<1; no endpoint, general rank-two or other measures claim.
